topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Well, there we were, just little sprats, and you planted that tree, didn’t you? Right there in the corner of the field, where the sun casts its warm embrace come noon. I thought it’d grow for ages, become a grand old thing, shading the younger ones and maybe even the grandkids. But sometimes, the land has its own mind, especially when crops are scarce and the mill needs repair. Still, it’s a good day, hear me? A good day to remember the fun of planting and the laughter that followed. Maybe we’ll plant another, a new chapter under the sky’s watching eye. After all, the earth is always ready for a new seed, isn’t she?
